newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab land dealers in hospital after PLO arrest.
newsitem.headline: Arab land dealers in hospital after PLO arrest.

text.p: PLO police brought two Palestinian land dealers to a Hebron hospital on Monday after holding them in prison for several days, Palestinian witnesses said.
They said it appeared the two, residents of the Hebron area in the West Bank, had been beaten while in custody. A Palestinian official said he knew of no such incident.
"I have not been informed of any such cases. I will check it," the Palestinian Authority's prosecutor general Khaled al-Kidra told Reuters.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule Authority, concerned over an Israeli government drive to expand Jewish settlements in the West Bank, has said the death penalty could be imposed on anyone who sold land to Jews, citing Jordanian law which once banned such sales.
Israel has described the measure as racist.
Palestinian security officials are holding at least 12 Arabs on suspicion of violating the ban, an official said this week.
Last week, the United States strongly criticised Arafat after an Israeli newspaper quoted him as backing the decision to enforce the death penalty.

Israel has linked the ban on land sales with the recent killings of two Palestinian land dealers found dead in the West Bank. The Authority, which says the law is applied by the courts and not vigilantes, has denied any involvement in the killings.

Palestinians say the purchase of land by Jews and Israeli settlement-building in Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank and Gaza pre-empts final peace talks on the fate of the areas where they hope to establish an independent state.
